title: Brazil's TCU captures R$426 million through its ALICE tender-analysis robot in 2021
summary: TCU says its ALICE tender-analysis robot captured R$426m in 2021 (R$194m in 2020); specific cases reported only via press
account: The Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) operates ALICE, a text-mining robot that reads federal tender notices and electronic-auction records daily and sends auditors a list of possible irregularities; trade press in 2017 and 2018 expanded the name as “Análise de Licitações e Editais”, while the TCU's own July 2020 release calls it the “Sistema de Análise de Licitações e Contratos (Alice)”. In its 4 March 2022 statement on 2021 control benefits, the TCU reported that the value captured through the Alice system was R$426 million in 2021 against R$194 million in 2020; only the year is given, so 1 January 2021 is used. Trade press in September 2017 quoted TCU auditor Valéria Nakano that Alice found two DNIT notices worth R$39 million for maintaining BR-153 stretches already under concession, blocked by an acórdão within two months; that acórdão could not be retrieved, so the example is unverified.
purpose: Daily automated screening of federal procurement notices to direct external-control auditors to likely irregularities
system: ALICE, expanded as 'Análise de Licitações e Editais' in 2017 and 2018 press reports and named 'Sistema de Análise de Licitações e Contratos (Alice)' in the TCU's July 2020 release, with companion tools SOFIA and MONICA; evolved into ALICE 360 by 2026
developer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), in-house
deployer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU); also shared with DNIT and the Ministry of Infrastructure under a 2020 agreement
domain: Public administration: external audit and procurement control

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: aggregate program figure with no discrete attributable event.
General benefit without an event: the R$426 million is an annual total of control benefits credited to the Alice system, not a single verified event.
General benefit without an event: aggregate; the TCU's own benefit-measurement methodology, not an independent evaluation.

ai_role.statement: The TCU attributes the 2021 figure to control actions supported by the Alice system under its benefit-measurement method (“o segundo de fato reflete o benefício calculado, que resultou da ação de controle e foi medido”); no independent evaluation or counterfactual was found. The 2017 DNIT/BR-153 example rests on a trade-press interview with a TCU auditor; the TCU acórdão was not located because the court's search application is JavaScript-only and its public API path returned 404. Developer and deployer are the same public body.

produced_by: Daily text-mining of the Diário Oficial and Comprasnet notices by Alice with e-mailed alerts to auditors
Low-cost follow-up by auditors (phone call, e-mail, ofício) or formal acórdão when needed
Agencies withdrawing, annulling or redoing flawed notices after contact
must_hold: Structured publication of notices on federal systems
Auditor capacity to act on the daily list
A benefit-measurement method that records actual, not potential, benefits

echoes.setting: The CGU's ALICE (Analisador de Licitações, Contratos e Editais), which the CGU says it developed: R$257.25 million saved in concluded 2024 audits (CGU, 30 December 2024)

TCE-MG version of Alice: in December 2022 TCE-MG published the result of an audit covering 2,297 state and municipal tenders in August 2022 alone, with corrections worth R$91,723,011.31 (Atricon, 28 June 2023; publication month only)
TCU Acórdão 1.145/2026 notes ALICE 360's move to intensive AI use; no outcome figures given (Zênite summary)

paired_incident.title: IRS Audited Black Taxpayers More Frequently Reportedly Due to Algorithm
paired_incident.basis: IRS audit-selection algorithm, an audit body's targeting tool like TCU's ALICE, skewed audits toward Black taxpayers, harming the taxpayers the audit function serves.

headline: TCU's ALICE tender-analysis robot captures R$426m in 2021

later.note: A TCU plenary ruling of 6 May 2026 (Acórdão 1.145/2026) records that the tool, now called Alice 360, has moved to intensive use of AI, with LLM-based query screens; no outcome figures are given.
later.quote: As evoluções incrementais já implementadas no Alice 360 incluem a transição das telas de consulta para sistemas baseados em Modelos de Linguagem de Grande Escala (LLM).
